title: US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers
content: The U.S. government is helping fund projects to bring nuclear reactors back online in an attempt to provide more energy capacity to AI data centers.

content: $35 billion worth of Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 GPUs have been bought by Chinese trio Tencent, Alibaba and ByteDance, with demand far exceeding Nvidia's planned production, according to report.

title: Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis
content: A hobbyist converted a SK hynix 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM kit they got off Facebook Marketplace for $120 into a DDR5-7800 desktop kit.

title: Pick up this DDR5 gaming PC for only $899
content: Pick up a brand-new iBuypower Slate PC for just $899, a great entry-level gaming PC option for 1080p gaming.

title: Ukraine rescues wounded soldier using drone in daring 'world's first' UAV evacuation of a human
content: The Ukrainian military is claiming a world’s first after using an unmanned drone to rescue an injured soldier on the eastern Kharkiv front.

title: Unimicron chairman sees substrate sizes reaching 14x current scale by 2030
content: TPCA Show 2026 officially opened, with Unimicron Chairman Shan-Chieh Chien saying in his opening address that solving the three major challenges facing AI accelerators in high-performance computing (HPC) will require more than semiconductor process scaling. Advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration technologies must be introduced in parallel, significantly raising the technical requirements for the PCB and substrate industries.

title: Jensen Huang urges Germany to embrace physical AI at Berlin summit
content: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urged German businesses to embrace AI at an industry summit in Berlin on October 19, aiming to revive the economy and modernize industry. Huang specifically called on Germany's automotive and industrial machinery sectors to adopt physical AI by leveraging the country's extensive manufacturing data and expertise.

title: Global Tek's new Thailand plant enters trial production in 3Q26, targeting AI liquid cooling and aerospace opportunities
content: Global Tek Industrial held an opening ceremony on the 20th for its Super Smart Manufacturing Park in Chonburi, Thailand. Spanning 177,600 square meters, the facility is the group's largest single production base. Having entered trial production in the third quarter of 2026, the plant will expand beyond existing automotive orders to incorporate high-value-added products such as AI liquid cooling and aerospace components, fulfilling customer demand for non-China supply chains.

title: Intel requests FCC waiver from US foreign robot ban, citing impact on US chipmaking
content: Intel has asked the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for a waiver to the US ban on advanced foreign robots, citing worries that its machines will not receive equipment updates, which could hinder its ability to produce semiconductors in the US. The request comes after the US banned imports of foreign-made robots in July.

title: Chief Telecom starts NT$3.3 billion AI data center in Taiwan
content: Chief Telecom broke ground on a new AI data center at the Central Taiwan Science Park on the 20th, committing approximately NT$3.3 billion (US$101.7 million) to a facility expected to begin operations in the second half of 2028. The project is intended to extend the company's data center growth, as its Lianyun AI Intelligent Data Center is projected to reach full capacity in 2027.

title: AI server demand lifts Tongtai drilling orders through 2027
content: Tongtai Machine & Tool said it had order visibility for its printed circuit board (PCB) drilling equipment through the end of 2027 as AI infrastructure demand increased pressure on high-end board production. The Taiwan-based machine tool maker presented its latest solutions at the Taiwan Printed Circuit Association Show 2026, highlighting CCD high-precision drilling machines and an unmanned drilling-station system for AI server boards and IC substrates.

title: AUO selects glass substrate specs for semiconductor processes, not size rivalry
content: AUO is tailoring its glass core substrate specifications specifically to semiconductor process requirements rather than competing on panel dimensions with Innolux, according to Chairman and CEO Paul Peng. The company aims to leverage its glass-processing expertise to supply critical components and technologies to outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) leaders such as ASE Technology Holding and Powertech Technology.

title: Taiwan anchors US chip revival, SEMICON West spotlights trusted partners
content: SEMICON West 2026 wrapped up in San Francisco last week, with US officials, industry executives, equipment and materials suppliers, and workforce-development partners repeatedly highlighting Taiwan as a critical partner in rebuilding US semiconductor manufacturing. Taiwan's role spans investment, process technology, supply-chain expertise, and talent development.

title: AI servers drive TVS and ESD demand for Yea Shin Tech
content: AI servers are driving demand for power components, transient voltage suppressors (TVS), and electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection devices. Yea Shin Technology, a subsidiary of Eris Technology, will begin trading on Taiwan's emerging stock market on October 23 and plans to raise the share of 6-inch wafers in its capacity from 35% to more than 50%, as its TVS products enter the international AI server supply chain.

title: Thermaltake expands AI workstation lineup on edge AI demand
content: Thermaltake is targeting the growing edge AI market with a new workstation lineup. Chairman Kenny Lin said the company has transformed from a gaming components maker into an AI PC and workstation systems provider. The company plans to launch three product lines in the second half of 2026 and aims for AI-related products to contribute 5% to 10% of revenue in 2027.

title: Samsung's HBM4 supply lock-in exposes limits of China's CXMT as Apple and Tesla seek DRAM alternatives
content: Samsung Electronics is expected to enter 2027 with approximately 80% of its planned memory production secured under long-term contracts, reinforcing its pricing position while China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) expands capacity and attracts attention from US tech companies seeking alternative DRAM suppliers.

title: Daeduck Electronics targets 2029 ceramic substrates for AI packaging
content: South Korean substrate maker Daeduck Electronics is accelerating development of ceramic core substrates (CCS) to address warpage and thermal-management challenges as AI semiconductor packages grow larger. The company is conducting performance and internal reliability assessments, plans to advance samples and customer evaluations in 2027 and 2028, and is targeting mass production in 2029, with ceramic cores serving as a material alternative to glass cores for next-generation large-area packages.

title: Genius Electronic Optical partners with 3M on EBO development
content: Genius Electronic Optical (GSEO), a leading manufacturer of optical lenses and precision optical components, has entered into a strategic partnership with 3M to develop, manufacture and expand production capacity for 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) solutions. As part of the deal, 3M will invest NT$4.8 billion (US$147.1 million) through a private placement and is expected to complete the transaction in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: Hygon's revenue jumps 58% on AI chip demand, but growth slows amid 51% stock slump
content: China's Hygon Information Technology reported a 57.58% increase in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, reflecting sustained demand for domestic high-performance processors and AI computing chips. Yet slower quarterly growth, mounting R&D expenditure and a steep share-price correction have highlighted the gap between the company's operating performance and market expectations.

title: Powertip Technology transitions into a solutions provider as demand and costs rise
content: Powertip Technology is transitioning from a module design and supply company to a solutions provider. The company has seen rising demand in the first half of 2026 as the electronics and manufacturing industries faced higher material costs, which it aims to control by negotiating price adjustments with its customers.
